flags: F-03 3073 pixels INSIDE the official footprint carry the float32 sentinel -3.4028235e+38 in at least one of the 19 bands (mag_anom, rtp, tmi_hg, geod_2ndinv, iso_grav_anom_slope, tc, geod_shearrate, geod_dilaterate, tmi_vg, deq_n100a15, iso_grav_anom_vg, det_elev, iso_grav_anom, tmi, depth_to_base_surf, ieq_n100a15, cond_surf, iso_grav_anom_hg, det_elev_slope). Any submission that lets a derived value propagate from these pixels is rejected with 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]'. gems22.submission.sanitise() forces them to 0.0 before clipping.

F-04 IRREGULARITY: the mirrored 'example_submission.tif' (= data/sample_submission.tif, sha256 2176d08e485aa2cd) contains 60988 pixels equal to 1.0, exactly the 60988 positive pixels of labels.tif.  The problem description says the sample 'predicts total fault absence'.  The file is still a valid FORMAT template (CRS/shape/transform/dtype/nodata all match), so it is used here only for the footprint mask and the write profile -- never as a prediction.

F-06 The 19 competition bands carry data_category values ['geodetic_strain', 'gravity_data', 'magnetic_data', 'seismic', 'subsurface', 'topographic'] -- there is NO radiometric family, although GeoDAWN is an 'airborne magnetic AND RADIOMETRIC' survey (USGS doi:10.5066/P93LGLVQ). The K/Th/U/TC grids from that same release are therefore genuinely orthogonal information and are used as external features.
